chapter_title: Concerning the Interpretation of the Five Words that are proclaimed in the Universe
chapter_note: This chapter fragment is dominated by dialogue-frame and sect-referential setup (Baptists / “Purified Ones”). The oldest recoverable layer appears only as brief enumerative identifications of the “words” with Manichaean cosmological beings (Father; Third Ambassador). The interpretive hook (“they call it by this name”) suggests the teaching is being applied to contemporary sectarian terminology, so the seam likely falls between the sectarian naming and the bare cosmological identifications.

paragraphs.temporal_note: Hagiographic/dialogue apparatus: “Once again…”, “disciples… questioned”, “apostle”, plus explicit anchoring to contemporary sects (“Baptists”, “Purified Ones”) and their terminology. This is editorial framing, not substrate exposition.

paragraphs.core_text: the Father, the l[ife ...] this unnameable, whom no one [...] his name.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed the leading interpretive/application clause (“[...] call it by this name is…”) which functions as a bridge from sectarian naming to the cosmological identification; retained only the impersonal identification of the first ‘word’ with the unnameable Father/Life.
paragraphs.temporal_note: What remains is a bare cosmological naming (“the Father… this unnameable”) characteristic of core expository diction; the excised lead-in ties the line to external groups’ naming practice, which is a later interpretive application.

paragraphs.core_text: The second [word is the Thir]d Ambassador [...] of life, whom they also call the father of [...] [...] the first Father.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Systematic enumerative identification (“The second word is…”) mapping a ‘word’ to a defined cosmological being (Third Ambassador). No explicit institutional/pastoral address or NT citation; reads like a fragment of an older five-fold list, though transmitted here in an interpretive chapter context.
